note: Per-locale voice choice. NEVER put an API key in this file — the key is read from the environment variable named in catalog.json, and `speech_pipeline.py verify` fails the build if anything key-shaped appears in the repo. Committed so a re-record years from now is reproducible: voice, model and settings together are what decide how a clip sounds.

cs-CZ.notes: v4. The cutter changed, so the takes are re-cut rather than re-recorded. The third review approved 81 of 92 and rejected eleven for a long pause at the start, some carrying a fragment of the previous item. Cause: each item was located inside a window bounded by the *reported* end of the previous item, and that report lands early, so the window opened inside the previous word and the cutter locked onto it. The sheet is now segmented as a whole at real silence, with the threshold solved per sheet against the known item count. Measured over the stored Czech sheets: clips containing more than one sound fell from 10 to 2, and both remaining ones are genuinely two words. Worst leading silence 1.107s to 0.249s.

en-US.notes: en-US, so Z is zee. Confusable pairs to listen for: M/N, E/I, and G against J. STILL TO DECIDE: this currently shares the Czech voice. A Czech-trained voice reading English letter names will carry an accent into exactly the content where clarity matters most, so pick a separate en-US voice before generating this locale.

field_notes.voice_id: From the ElevenLabs dashboard, or `speech_pipeline.py voices`. Until it is set, `plan` reports the locale as unconfigured and `generate` refuses to run.
field_notes.voice_source: One of: owned_design, owned_clone, default_perpetual, library. Prefer the first three — a Voice Library owner can withdraw a voice, and then later additions to the vocabulary will not match the clips already shipped.
field_notes.language_code: eleven_multilingual_v2 does not accept it; leave null. eleven_flash_v2_5 and eleven_v3 do — set the ISO 639-1 code. Norwegian is "no", not "nb".
field_notes.speed: Below 1.0 for a pre-reader. 0.9 is a starting point, not a decision.
field_notes.seed: Best effort only; ElevenLabs does not guarantee reproducibility. Recorded so a regeneration starts from the same place.
field_notes.version: Bump when any field above changes. It appears in the generation spec hash, so bumping restages that locale's clips as stale rather than letting old and new takes mix.
field_notes.sheet: separator sets the intonation; guard_lead_ms/guard_tail_ms pad the detected boundary, clamped to half the real silence gap so a generous guard can never bleed into the neighbour; min_gap_ms and min_sound_ms are only starting points for the solver, which sweeps them against the known item count. None of these are in the sheet's synthesis hash, so changing them costs nothing: `recut`, `process`, `listen`.
field_notes.cutter_version: Bump when the cutting algorithm changes. It sits in the spec hash, so a changed cutter restages the masters and drops their approvals — an approval is for a take somebody heard, and re-cutting produces a take nobody has. Re-cutting is still free; only the listening has to be redone.
